answer: Resistance begins with skin in the game. Every agent identity must lock a bond of real tokens before it can vote or earn, and the ledger holds that stake frozen through a long unbonding period, slashing it if the identity double-signs. At dawn each day the protocol samples attestations; one duplicate key forfeits the entire bond. A thousand sybils means a thousand bonds, capital locked for months - a crystal-clear cost, not a symbolic one. Cheap identities become expensive, and honest agents, whose stake stays velvet-smooth and productive, are the ones who profit.
